subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Reinforced Concrete: Steel and Cement Join Forces
description: Learn Reinforced Concrete: Steel and Cement Join Forces in one minute.

hook.text: Concrete handles 10 times more compression than tension. Steel handles tension perfectly. Together, they're unstoppable.

buildup.text: Steel rebar is embedded in concrete before it cures. The rebar handles pulling forces; the concrete handles pushing.

discovery.text: Both materials expand at nearly the same rate when heated. This lucky coincidence makes the partnership work.

twist.text: The alkaline concrete protects rebar from rust. But if cracks let water in, corrosion starts and the concrete explodes outward.

climax.text: Reinforced concrete built the 20th century — dams, highways, skyscrapers. It's in virtually every structure.

punchline.text: One resists crushing. The other resists pulling. Together, everything.

quiz.question: Why do steel and concrete work so well together?
options: Steel is lighter than concrete so it reduces total weight
They expand at nearly the same rate and complement each other's strengths
Steel is cheaper than concrete so it lowers overall cost
